articles.title: Abu Dhabi Court Grants Binance $6.5 Billion Freezing Order After Hack
articles.excerpt: Circle, World Liberty Financial and 16 other firms must keep stolen tokens frozen, court papers show. Tether is not covered. A hearing is set for Dec. 1.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Wednesday it obtained a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Courts against the unidentified attackers behind its Oct. 29 hack, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-binance-freezing-court-order-adgm-crypto-october-hack-443491) and [Reuters](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/uae-court-orders-freeze-crypto-tokens-stolen-binance-wallets) reported.

The $6.5 billion is the maximum value the order covers. Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the roughly $6.34 billion in assets hit by the hack was frozen or intercepted by third parties. U.S. authorities have attributed the attack to North Korea, Reuters reported.

**Who the Order Covers**

Circle, World Liberty Financial and 16 other companies must keep tokens tied to the hack frozen pending further proceedings, according to court documents seen by Reuters. They also may not lend, swap or mix those tokens with other assets. The court said the 18 firms are not accused of wrongdoing.

Tether, which has said it froze $1.5 billion in USDT, was not named in the order. "In consultation with the relevant authorities, we will work directly with Binance in respect of reissuing the tokens," a Tether spokesperson said, according to Reuters.

**How a Freezing Order Works on a Blockchain**

A freezing order bars the people it targets from moving assets up to a set value. Stablecoin issuers such as Circle and Tether can lock tokens in their own contracts. Binance said some issuers and exchanges require a court order before they release frozen funds.

Binance's lawyers at Gibson Dunn said the orders can be served via the blockchain. They also said a "living list" of 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets will be updated as the funds move, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-binance-freezing-court-order-adgm-crypto-october-hack-443491).

**Responses**

Binance said in a blog post that it had absorbed the loss and made customers whole, Reuters reported. A World Liberty Financial spokesman said the company "acted decisively to protect our users and our partners." Circle did not immediately respond to Reuters.

A further hearing is set for Dec. 1, when the court will consider whether the asset-specific freeze should continue and on what terms.

*In our opinion: The figure to track is the $2.85 billion that third parties have already frozen, since the $6.5 billion is a legal ceiling. A court order gives cautious issuers the paperwork they asked for, and that is the practical gain here. The Dec. 1 hearing will show whether the freeze holds, and whether Tether's separate route returns funds faster.*

articles.title: Fed Minutes Show Almost All Officials Expect More Rate Hikes
articles.excerpt: The October minutes show a 10-2 vote to hold at 3.75%-4%, two dissents for a hike, and wide concern that AI spending is feeding inflation.
articles.body_md:
Almost all Federal Reserve officials judged at their Oct. 27-28 meeting that further interest rate increases "would likely be appropriate," according to [minutes released Wednesday](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm). The committee still held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote.

Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, preferring a quarter-point hike at that meeting, the minutes show. A couple of officials said an increase of more than 25 basis points, or a quarter of a percentage point, could warrant consideration at the next meeting if inflation data came in unfavorable.

**How Fed Minutes Work**

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the Fed group that sets short-term rates, publishes minutes three weeks after each decision. They summarize the debate without naming speakers. They count heads in words, from "a couple" up to "almost all." Officials who backed the October hold pointed to the benefit of gathering more information first, the minutes said.

**AI Spending Enters the Inflation Debate**

"Many participants viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk," the minutes said. The worry is that the data-center boom raises demand faster than capacity can expand. Officials also looked at the debt behind it: most said AI-related debt "had grown rapidly," much of it through "complex and opaque financing structures." Several noted the staff view that the financial system remained resilient and banks were well capitalized.

**From Rates to Crypto**

A rate hike raises what savers earn on cash and Treasury bills. That raises the bar for assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin. Bitcoin traded at $62,196 at 5:55 p.m. ET, down 3.9% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

Futures markets fully price a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/fed-minutes-october-2026.html), citing CME Group's FedWatch tool.

*In our opinion: The October hold read as patient on the day, but the minutes show a committee with its coat already on, waiting for one more look at the data. The new wrinkle is AI: the Fed now treats the data-center boom as both an inflation source and a debt risk, which ties the rate story crypto traders follow to tech balance sheets. The date to circle is Dec. 9, and the detail to watch is whether more than "a couple" of officials back a half-point move.*

articles.title: Variational Raises $110 Million at $1.5 Billion Valuation, Led by Bain
articles.excerpt: The on-chain derivatives platform says its Omni app has handled $475 billion in volume since early 2025, with more than half now in stocks and commodities.
articles.body_md:
Variational, an on-chain derivatives platform, said Wednesday it raised $110 million in a Series B round led by Bain Capital Crypto at a $1.5 billion valuation, according to a [company release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116481769/en/Variational-Raises-%24110M-Series-B-at-%241.5B-Valuation-To-Scale-On-Chain-Access-To-Global-Markets). Dragonfly, HSG and Peak XV also took part, [Reuters reported](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/variational-valued-15-billion-bain-led-funding-round).

The round more than doubles the $50 million Series A that Dragonfly led in [May](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260520402312/en/Variational-Secures-%2450M-to-Bring-Liquidity-from-Traditional-Markets-To-Crypto).

**What Omni Does**

Variational runs Omni, a trading platform offering leveraged bets on more than 550 crypto and traditional markets, including stocks, indexes, commodities and currencies. A derivative is a contract whose value tracks another asset, so a trader can bet on gold or an index without owning it.

Omni charges no trading fees. Instead, an in-house liquidity provider quotes every price and earns the spread (the gap between the buy and sell price), the company said. That provider pulls prices from crypto exchanges and traditional firms, including what Variational called "a tier-1 market maker."

**The Traction Numbers**

Since launching in early 2025, Omni has processed more than $475 billion in volume and holds more than $1.3 billion in open interest, the value of all open positions, the company said. Reuters carried the same figures. Variational said more than half of daily volume is now in traditional markets, and that it has more than 100,000 accounts.

The company said the money will lift open-interest caps that traders keep hitting and add hundreds of new markets, with 24/7 swaps trading and a trading API planned.

**Open Questions**

All traction figures come from Variational and have not been independently audited. The release does not say which countries can use Omni or how its stock and commodity contracts are regulated. Leveraged trading can multiply losses as well as gains.

*In our opinion: The company is betting that traders want stock and oil exposure on crypto rails, and the volume split suggests some already do. The risk sits with the in-house liquidity provider on the other side of every trade, so how it is capitalized matters more than the valuation. Watch whether Variational publishes audited figures and says where Omni is licensed.*

articles.title: Visa Brings Stablecoin Funding for Visa Direct Payouts to Asia-Pacific
articles.excerpt: Singapore's dtcpay is the first pilot partner. Businesses fund payouts with stablecoins while recipients get local currency, Visa said.
articles.body_md:
Visa said Wednesday it plans to let eligible clients in Asia-Pacific fund cross-border payouts on its Visa Direct network, which it says reaches more than 18 billion endpoints, with stablecoins, according to a [Visa press release](https://www.visa.com.sg/about-visa/newsroom/press-releases/visa-direct-advances-stablecoin-powered-money-movement-in-asia-pacific.html).

Singapore payments firm dtcpay is the first pilot partner. The people getting paid won't touch crypto: recipients still receive local currency, Visa said.

**What Prefunding Means**

Visa Direct is Visa's system for pushing money out in real time, to a card, bank account or wallet. A business that sends payouts through it has to put money in first, which is called prefunding. Visa said stablecoin prefunding gives clients more flexibility in managing short-term liquidity.

Under the new setup, a client can fund that balance with a stablecoin, a token built to hold a steady value such as one U.S. dollar. Stablecoins move on blockchains around the clock. Triple-A, a Singapore-based stablecoin payments firm, said in a [separate release](https://www.triple-a.io/newsroom/stablecoin-prefunding-visa-direct-asia-pacific) that it handles the conversion, compliance screening and settlement, so payment providers can fund Visa Direct outside traditional banking hours.

Visa said it does not provide regulated digital asset services itself and that a licensed partner handles that side. It did not name which stablecoins the Asia-Pacific pilot will use, and gave no volumes or fees.

**From U.S. Launch to Asia**

Visa began testing stablecoin prefunding in 2025. The service went into commercial use in the U.S. in October with Inyo Global, Visa said, and [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-visa-direct-extend-stablecoin-prefunding-cross-border-payouts-asia-pacific-443457) reported that version uses Circle's USDC.

"Asia Pacific already accounts for nearly a third of global cross-border payment flows," Triple-A CEO Eric Barbier said in the release.

Total stablecoin supply stood at $287.8 billion on Wednesday, down $2.59 billion from a week earlier, according to [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins).

*In our opinion: Banks close for the weekend, and blockchains don't, which is the whole pitch here in one sentence. The firms that gain are payout providers that would otherwise wait on a bank wire to top up a balance on a Friday night. The number to watch is how much money actually flows through the pilot, and which stablecoins Visa names when it does.*

articles.title: Fed's Waller Says a Half-Point Hike Is Probably Needed in December
articles.excerpt: Futures price a quarter-point Fed hike on Dec. 9. Waller told CNBC the Fed may need to double that, or spell out a January move, to curb inflation.
articles.body_md:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that a half-point interest rate increase is probably needed at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting, telling [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/federal-reserve-governor-christopher-waller.html) the central bank "might need to, like, shock people."

Futures already fully price a quarter-point hike in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool as cited by CNBC. A half-point move would be double that.

**Waller's Two Options**

Waller said the Fed could instead raise rates by a quarter point and clearly flag another hike in January, either in its statement or at Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/waller-says-on-cnbc-the-fed-needs-to-get-more-aggressive-in-inflation-response-5036212). Without that, he said, "you have to go 50 in December." CNBC noted Warsh has opposed that kind of forward guidance.

"I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," Waller said. He told the network the Fed needs to reverse its three quarter-point cuts from 2025 and may have to go further.

Reuters reported Waller is worried that businesses now treat 3% inflation as normal and pass it on to customers.

**How a Bigger Hike Reaches Crypto**

The Fed's benchmark rate sets the floor for what cash and short-term Treasuries pay. When that floor rises, assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin, have to compete with a safer return. Crypto's basis trade, which pays traders for holding bitcoin against short futures, now yields about 3% to 5% a year, near or below Treasury yields, according to Talos data cited by [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/18/bitcoin-drops-as-nvidia-earnings-report-drives-stock-index-futures-higher).

Bitcoin traded at $62,311 at 11:47 a.m. ET, down 2.2% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

Not every official agrees. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday, "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," CNBC reported. The Fed releases minutes of its October meeting at 2 p.m. ET Wednesday.

*In our opinion: The Fed raised rates once in September and held in October, so a half-point move would mark a clear change in pace. Waller's real target is the gap between what markets price and what he thinks is needed. The October minutes due at 2 p.m. ET are the first look at how many colleagues lean his way before the Dec. 9 decision.*

articles.title: UK Inflation Rises to 3.6% as Diesel Hits a Record 199.5p a Litre
articles.excerpt: UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5%, as motor fuel costs climbed 33.2%, the ONS said, after this month's Bank of England hike.
articles.body_md:
UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in the 12 months to October, up from 3.5% in September, the [Office for National Statistics](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/bulletins/consumerpriceinflation/october2026) said Wednesday. That matches the rate a year earlier, and the ONS said CPI was last higher in September 2025.

**Fuel Did Most of the Lifting**

Motor fuel prices were 33.2% higher than a year earlier, the biggest annual jump since July 2022, the ONS said. Diesel averaged 199.5 pence a litre in October, the highest since the agency's records began in January 1996. Petrol averaged 174.7 pence, its highest since August 2022.

Restaurants and hotels pulled the other way. Prices there rose 3.4% over the year, down from 3.8% in September, as hotel rates fell.

Core inflation, which strips out energy, food, alcohol and tobacco, was 2.8% and little changed from September. Services inflation held at 3.7%, while goods inflation rose to 3.5% from 3.2%.

**How the Number Is Built**

The Consumer Prices Index (CPI) tracks the cost of a fixed basket of goods and services that households buy, from bread to bus fares. The headline rate compares October's basket with the same month a year earlier. Core inflation removes the most volatile items to show the slower trend underneath.

**What the Bank of England Faces**

The reading matched the forecast of economists polled by Reuters, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/uk-inflation-cpi-fuel-prices.html). The Bank of England raised its rate earlier this month for the first time in three years and warned inflation could reach 5% by mid-2027, CNBC said. Traders were pricing about an 80% chance of another hike at the bank's December meeting, according to the same report.

Britain imports more energy than it produces, which leaves it exposed to oil shocks such as the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, CNBC noted. Oil has eased from wartime highs above $100 a barrel, CNBC said, though it remains elevated.

The ONS publishes November figures on Dec. 16.

*In our opinion: The number that matters is the gap between 3.6% headline inflation and 2.8% core: fuel is doing most of the damage while the slower trend holds steady. Drivers and diesel-heavy businesses carry the cost at nearly 2 pounds a litre. The Bank of England's December decision and the Dec. 16 data will show whether the rate hike becomes a pair.*

articles.title: DBS and Circle Open 24/7 USDC Minting for Asian Institutions
articles.excerpt: DBS said eligible institutional clients in Asia can now mint and redeem Circle's USDC directly through the bank, with dollar settlement around the clock.
articles.body_md:
Singapore's DBS Bank said Wednesday that eligible institutional clients in Asia can mint and redeem Circle's USDC stablecoin directly through the bank, with dollar settlement available 24 hours a day, according to a [joint announcement](https://www.dbs.com/newsroom/DBS_and_Circle_expand_institutional_access_to_USDC_in_Asia).

USDC had about $69.3 billion in circulation as of Wednesday, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-18-dbs-circle-usdc-asia-442970), making it the second-largest stablecoin after Tether's USDT.

**What Minting Through a Bank Means**

A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a steady value, here one U.S. dollar. Minting means handing over dollars and receiving newly created USDC; redeeming is the reverse. Institutions can also buy USDC from other holders on trading venues, which is called the secondary market. DBS said the new route lets clients rely less on that market and move between dollars and USDC outside banking hours and cutoff times.

DBS does not issue the token. USDC is issued by regulated Circle affiliates, and DBS provides the banking side.

**What Was Not Disclosed**

The announcement gave no fees, volumes, client names or list of countries, and did not define which institutions qualify. It said the service targets treasury, settlement and liquidity management.

"By supporting USDC, alongside other trusted tokenised money instruments, we are providing institutions greater choice in how they move and manage value," said Evy Theunis, head of digital assets in DBS's institutional banking group. Circle Chief Commercial Officer Kash Razzaghi said "financial institutions are increasingly looking for trusted ways to access stablecoins."

Both companies take part in Project BLOOM, a Monetary Authority of Singapore effort to make different forms of tokenized money work together. Circle reported that USDC averaged $73.3 billion in circulation in the third quarter, up 8% from a year earlier, The Block said.

*In our opinion: The question worth chasing is volume, and DBS kept that number to itself, which leaves the headline doing most of the work for now. Circle gains a bank on-ramp in Asia at a time when USDC supply is down about $6 billion this year. Watch for the first named clients and markets, and for whether supply moves back toward the $73.3 billion third-quarter average.*

articles.title: Scottish Hacker Gets Six Years in $11.6 Million SIM-Swap Crypto Case
articles.excerpt: Tyler Buchanan, 24, got 72 months in U.S. federal prison over a phishing and SIM-swap scheme that took at least $11.6 million in crypto, prosecutors said.
articles.body_md:
A federal judge in Santa Ana, California, sentenced Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, to 72 months in prison on Tuesday for a scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto from U.S. victims, the [U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California](https://www.publicnow.com/view/E0493E0D41512772CC7756101A631110F135263D) said.

Buchanan pleaded guilty on April 17 to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of aggravated identity theft. U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb set a restitution hearing for Dec. 11. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant sentenced in the case, prosecutors said.

**How the Scheme Worked, According to the Plea Agreement**

From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and others sent hundreds of text messages to employees of at least a dozen companies, including telecom, tech and crypto firms, prosecutors said. The texts linked to fake login pages that captured usernames and passwords.

The group then used data taken from those companies to find individual crypto holders and carry out SIM swaps. In a SIM swap, a criminal tricks a mobile carrier into moving a victim's phone number to a SIM card the criminal controls. That lets the criminal receive the one-time security codes sent by text and get into the victim's accounts.

At his plea in April, prosecutors put the losses at $8 million. The figure has since risen to at least $11.6 million. The largest single theft was $1.67 million in December 2022, the [BBC reported](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm87987w1qz5o), citing prosecutors.

**Who Else Was Sentenced**

Buchanan was charged alongside four American co-defendants, who have all pleaded guilty and are serving prison terms, the BBC said. U.S. authorities have linked the defendants to Scattered Spider, a loose group of mostly young, English-speaking hackers blamed for several large corporate breaches, the BBC said.

Prosecutors said the thefts had "severe, life-altering consequences" for victims. The prosecutors' release and the news reports Black Mint reviewed did not include a statement from Buchanan or his lawyer.

*In our opinion: The Dec. 11 restitution hearing is the next date that matters for victims, because it sets what they are owed out of at least $11.6 million taken. Security codes sent by text go to whoever controls the phone number, and in this case that was the thieves. Where an exchange offers an authenticator app or hardware key, that option does not depend on the carrier.*

articles.title: BOJ's Ueda Says Rate Hikes Should Continue as Policy Stays Easy
articles.excerpt: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament the bank should keep raising its 1.25% policy rate because financial conditions are still easy.
articles.body_md:
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament on Wednesday, Nov. 18, Tokyo time, that the central bank should keep raising interest rates, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/ueda-says-boj-will-weigh-if-underlying-inflation-becomes-anchored-5034497). Japan's policy rate stands at 1.25%.

The yen matters to crypto because of borrowing. For years, cheap yen loans helped fund bets on higher-yielding assets abroad. When Japanese rates rise, that funding costs more, and some of those trades get closed.

**Ueda Points to Easy Financial Conditions**

"Given that financial conditions are still accommodative, it would be appropriate to continue raising the policy rate," Ueda said, according to Reuters. He added that the bank wants underlying inflation anchored around its 2% target over time.

He also addressed the government's planned cut to the consumption tax on food. Ueda said it would probably support growth by lifting households' real buying power, and that the BOJ would study its effect on underlying inflation once the details are final. [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/central-banks/ueda-keeps-december-hike-in-play-as-boj-wants-inflation-anchored-around-2/) reported that he expected the impact to stay limited but called it highly uncertain for now.

**How a Policy Rate Hike Works**

The policy rate is what the BOJ sets for overnight lending between banks. Raising it pushes up borrowing costs across the economy, from mortgages to company loans. "Accommodative" means rates are still low enough to encourage borrowing and spending, even after past hikes.

**What He Did Not Commit To**

Ueda did not name a date for the next move. At the Oct. 30 meeting, the BOJ held at 1.25% while saying underlying inflation had reached its target, and board member Hajime Takata voted for a hike to 1.5%, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bank-of-japan-to-hold-rates-signal-further-hikes-4985276) at the time. On emergency bond buying, Ueda said such operations could backfire if markets saw the BOJ as financing government spending: "In that case, long-term interest rates could become even more volatile."

The BOJ's next policy meeting is in December.

*In our opinion: Ueda repeated the bank's direction rather than adding anything new, so the December meeting and the food tax details now carry more weight. A higher Japanese rate makes yen-funded trades more expensive to hold, and crypto has been on the receiving end of those unwinds before. The number to watch is whether the BOJ moves the 1.25% rate next month.*

articles.title: Russia Lets Retail Investors Buy Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, Capped at 300,000 Rubles
articles.excerpt: A Bank of Russia rule in force since Nov. 17 lets retail buyers purchase BTC, ETH and USDT through licensed firms, capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary.
articles.body_md:
Retail investors in Russia can now buy bitcoin, ether and Tether's USDT through licensed intermediaries. A [Bank of Russia ordinance](https://www.cbr.ru/eng/press/event/?id=32966) took effect on Nov. 17, with a cap of 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary.

For crypto markets, this opens a legal on-ramp in a country whose retail buyers already trade offshore. Finam executive Dmitry Lesnov estimated that Russia makes up 15% to 20% of traffic on the largest Asian crypto exchanges, [Bitcoin Magazine reported](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/russia-retail-bitcoin-buying-starts), citing Vedomosti.

**Three Coins, One Test, a Ruble Cap**

The central bank said it chose the three assets on market value, average daily trading volume and at least five years of price history on foreign exchanges. Purchases can run through brokers, trust managers or crypto exchange offices, on an exchange or over the counter. Qualified investors face no cap and can access any crypto asset.

Every buyer, retail or not, must pass a test and read a risk disclosure first. The 300,000-ruble cap is about $3,600 at the central bank's official rate, per Bitcoin Magazine. At bitcoin's $64,364 price on [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) at 11:55 p.m. ET on Nov. 17, that buys about 0.056 BTC per intermediary per year.

**How the Cap Works**

The limit applies to each intermediary, not each person, so a buyer with accounts at two brokers could in principle buy up to the cap at each one. A "non-qualified investor" is Russia's legal term for an ordinary retail buyer who does not meet wealth or experience thresholds.

**Big Brokers Not Live Yet**

T-Bank and VTB were not yet offering crypto on launch day, Bitcoin Magazine reported, citing TASS. Both are waiting on an industry testing standard that the central bank has not yet approved. Lesnov said the cap would significantly limit retail interest, according to the same report.

Moscow Exchange plans pilot trading in the three assets on Dec. 1, Bitcoin Magazine reported. The exchange and its clearing house have been under [U.S. Treasury sanctions](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2404) since June 2024.

*In our opinion: The cap is small next to the offshore trading Lesnov describes, so early volumes may say more about the test rollout than about demand. Russian retail buyers gain a legal domestic route, while the sanctions on Moscow Exchange keep foreign firms out of that venue. Watch the central bank's approval of the testing standard and the Dec. 1 exchange pilot; for now, the rulebook arrived before the buy button did.*

articles.title: Pentagon Fails Ninth Straight Audit of Over $4.8 Trillion
articles.excerpt: The inspector general issued a disclaimer of opinion. One retiree health fund got its first clean opinion; four more reviews are due in February.
articles.body_md:
The Pentagon failed to get a clean, department-wide financial audit for the ninth straight year, the inspector general said Monday, Nov. 16. The review covered more than $4.8 trillion in assets across nearly 30 components and involved about 1,500 auditors, the [inspector general's office](https://www.dodig.mil/News/Press-Release/) said.

Congress set a Dec. 31, 2028, deadline for a clean, or unqualified, opinion on the department's books. The requirement is in the fiscal 2024 National Defense Authorization Act, the [Government Accountability Office](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-25-107427) and a [Congressional Research Service primer](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/IF12627.html) both note.

### What a disclaimer of opinion means

A disclaimer of opinion means the department could not give auditors enough evidence to say whether its financial statements are reliable. That is not a finding that the figures are wrong, and it is not a passing grade. A clean, or unmodified, opinion means auditors had enough evidence to say the statements fairly present the department's finances.

### The audit's 2028 target, and a caution from the watchdog

The Medicare-Eligible Retiree Health Care Fund received its first unmodified opinion this month, the inspector general and the department said. The department said it also expects improved opinions in February on four more components. Those are the Navy Working Capital Fund, the Defense Information Systems Agency's general fund, the Defense Intelligence Agency and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.

"For the first time, by February 2027, we will have clean opinions on a majority of our assets and over 90% of our liabilities," Comptroller Jules W. Hurst III said in the [department's release](https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/4649444/new-dow-audit-progress-marks-breakthrough-toward-a-department-wide-clean-opinion/). Those shares include the opinions expected in January and February.

The inspector general's reports listed 14 material weaknesses in internal controls and five instances of noncompliance with laws and regulations. Brett Mansfield, the deputy inspector general for audit, said the apparent reduction "stems from consolidation, not resolution," [Just the News](https://justthenews.com/government/federal-agencies/pentagon-fails-financial-audit-ninth-consecutive-fiscal-year) reported.

Hurst said the department is consolidating 25 statements into eight and has hired an independent public accountant. Several component audits remain open, the inspector general said.

*In our opinion: A disclaimer is not proof that money is missing, and it is not a passing grade. After nine years, auditors still lack the evidence to sign the books, even as one fund earned its first clean opinion. The legal deadline is Dec. 31, 2028. Watch the four opinions due in February, and whether that strategy later yields a clean department-wide opinion for fiscal 2028.*

articles.title: World Bank to Test Circle's USDC and Citi Rails for Development Payouts
articles.excerpt: The World Bank Group said it will explore paying out development funds in USDC, with Citi linking bank rails and Circle minting and settling the stablecoin.
articles.body_md:
The World Bank Group said Tuesday it will explore using Circle's USDC stablecoin and Citi's banking network to send development money, building on a blockchain ledger already used by more than 350 projects in 96 countries, according to its [press release](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2026/11/17/world-bank-group-explores-regulated-stablecoins-to-modernize-payments-redirect-res).

The lender said the test will look at whether regulated dollar stablecoins can work alongside, or improve on, the way it pays out funds today. Citi would supply its links to existing bank rails, and Circle would mint and settle the funds in USDC, [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383485/world-bank-circle-citi-test-stablecoins-development-payments) reported, in line with the release.

### How the money moves now

World Bank disbursements currently run through correspondent banking: a chain of banks that each hold accounts with one another and pass an international payment along, one step at a time. A stablecoin is a token pegged one-to-one to the dollar and backed by reserves, so it can move on a blockchain at any hour. The catch is that someone still has to turn it back into local money at the other end, which is the job Citi's bank connections would fill.

The first phase will use an "intermediated and interoperable" model and is limited to borrower countries where digital assets are permitted, the release said. Other banks are expected to join later. No dollar amounts, launch date or list of countries were given.

The effort extends FundsChain, the World Bank's existing blockchain platform that lets everyone on a project see how money is spent. President Ajay Banga said the aim is that "a farmer gets paid before the harvest season ends."

USDC had a market value of about $68.9 billion at 5:47 p.m. ET, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/usdc). Circle and Citi are the only named partners.

*In our opinion: The release describes an exploration with no dollar figure attached, so the size of the test will matter more than the logos. Still, a lender that moves money into 96 countries is weighing a stablecoin against correspondent banking, a sign of how far regulated stablecoins have moved into mainstream finance. Watch which borrower countries sign on first and whether a second bank joins Citi.*

articles.title: Nvidia Posts $115.8 Billion Quarter and Guides to $130 Billion, Above Estimates
articles.excerpt: Nvidia's revenue rose 103% from a year earlier to $115.8 billion, above the $109.1 billion analysts expected, in its first report since Jensen Huang left as CEO.
articles.body_md:
Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the quarter ended Oct. 25, up 103% from a year earlier, and forecast about $130 billion for the current quarter, according to its [earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000088/q3fy27pr.htm) filed Tuesday. Both numbers topped Wall Street estimates.

Analysts had expected $109.10 billion in revenue and adjusted earnings of $2.48 a share, according to LSEG data cited by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q3-2027.html). Nvidia earned $2.68 a share on an adjusted basis. The $130 billion forecast, plus or minus 3%, compares with an average estimate of $125.1 billion.

It was the company's first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week, CNBC and [Investopedia](https://www.investopedia.com/nvidia-stock-rises-after-fy27-q3-revenue-net-profit-beat-expectations-nvda-earnings-12258779) reported.

### Where the money came from

- Data center: $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year earlier
- Edge computing: $8.2 billion, up 42%
- Net income: $65.3 billion, up 105%
- Adjusted gross margin: 74.9%

Data center sales are the chips and networking gear that cloud companies and AI labs buy to train and run models. Gross margin is the share of each sales dollar left after the cost of making the product. Nvidia guided that margin down to 71% to 72% next quarter. Its outlook assumes no data center compute sales to China, and the quarter includes an extra week.

Nvidia also returned $28.1 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends during the quarter.

The stock closed at $160.50, up 3.2%, and rose about 2% more in after-hours trading, CNBC reported. Bitcoin traded at $64,762 at 5:47 p.m. ET, down 1% in 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: A $6.7 billion revenue beat in the first report without Huang as CEO gives the board a strong opening answer on succession. For crypto readers, the open question is whether a firmer tech tape lifts appetite for risk more broadly. The next tell is whether Wednesday's session holds the after-hours gain, and whether the 71% margin guide becomes the new worry.*

articles.title: Solana Foundation Takes Majority Stake in CoinGecko, Plans Trading on the Site
articles.excerpt: The Solana Foundation now holds a majority interest in CoinGecko, which has 18 million registered users. Neither side disclosed the price or the exact stake.
articles.body_md:
The Solana Foundation now holds a majority interest in CoinGecko, the crypto price and data site with 18 million registered users, the foundation's chief product officer, Vibhu Norby, said Tuesday. Neither side disclosed the price or the exact size of the stake, according to [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/17/solana-foundation-takes-majority-stake-in-crypto-data-provider-coingecko) and [Unchained, via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/coingecko-gets-solana-foundation-backing-154535900.html).

The deal was announced at the foundation's Breakpoint conference in London. CoinGecko's [own announcement](https://www.coingecko.com/learn/next-chapter-of-growth-solana-foundation) says it is "backed by Solana Foundation" and lists three focus areas: data and API services, market research tools, and trading, which it describes as a capability it is "exploring."

### What changes for users

The foundation said it plans "on-platform trading powered by Solana" on CoinGecko's website, its GeckoTerminal tracker and its mobile app, Unchained reported. Norby also pointed to wider coverage of stocks and tokenized real-world assets, meaning shares, bonds and other traditional assets recorded on a blockchain.

According to the foundation, CoinGecko logs more than 50 million monthly sessions, and about 180,000 apps and businesses pull its prices through its API, a feed that lets other software request data automatically. CoinGecko said its website, app and API "will continue operating as usual" and that its methods for ranking and pricing coins will stay public.

CoinGecko was founded in 2014 by Bobby Ong and TM Lee. In January, CoinDesk reported that the company had hired the bank Moelis to explore a sale at a possible valuation near $500 million, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter. Binance bought rival CoinMarketCap in 2020.

CoinGecko and the foundation did not respond to CoinDesk's request for comment on the deal terms. Black Mint uses CoinGecko for the prices in its stories. Solana's SOL traded at $71.96 at 11:55 a.m. ET, up 1.3% in 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/solana).

*In our opinion: CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko now both sit under owners with a stake in what they rank: one an exchange, the other a blockchain's foundation. The promise to keep methods public is the part worth holding them to, because thousands of apps treat those prices as neutral. The first test comes when Solana trading goes live on the site: watch whether rankings, listings and default pages stay chain-neutral.*

articles.title: Fed's Waller Says Central Bank Money Must Stay at the Base of Tokenized Markets
articles.excerpt: In a New York speech, Fed Governor Christopher Waller backed several kinds of tokenized money competing, but said bank and Fed rails should remain the base for final settlement.
articles.body_md:
Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Tuesday that stablecoins, tokenized bank deposits and tokenized money market funds will likely coexist in blockchain markets, but that central bank money should remain "at the foundation of the system." He spoke in New York, according to the [Fed's published text](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/waller20261117a.htm).

Waller organized the speech around three questions: how tokenization is changing competition, how new services earn trust, and how payments connect to tokenized markets. He said the views were his own, not the Fed board's.

### Tokens, explained with poker chips

Waller defined tokenization by comparing it to a casino. Players swap cash for chips that work at the tables. A tokenized stock or dollar works the same way: the asset gets a digital form that can move on a blockchain. Smart contracts, pieces of code stored on the chain, can then release the payment and the asset at the same moment.

He gave the example of an investor buying a tokenized stock on a Saturday, when many banking systems are shut. With tokenized money, he said, both sides of the trade could settle together, cutting the risk that one party pays and the other doesn't deliver.

### Open questions on trust

Waller said the industry still has to answer who pays when fraudsters exploit smart contracts, who is responsible for lost keys and mistaken transfers, and what happens to assets left on abandoned "zombie chains." He pointed to the recent Binance breach as an example.

He also said "atomic" settlement, where a multi-step trade completes in full or not at all, shouldn't be the only model. Net and batch settlement, which fund only the difference owed, save cash for high-volume trading, he said.

The Fed's role, Waller said, is to supply core payment rails, watch financial-stability risks and act as a "connector and convener" where markets can't solve a problem alone. Bitcoin traded at $63,610 at 11:55 a.m. ET, down 1.5% in 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: This was neither a warning shot nor a green light. A Fed governor is now describing stablecoins and tokenized deposits as competitors in the same market, each with a use. The line to read twice keeps central bank money at the base, so the tokenized future still settles through the Fed's rails. Watch what comes out of his Sept. 18 payments roundtable and whether the Fed proposes anything concrete on access to those rails.*

articles.title: Seven Big Banks Reported $5.5 Billion in BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF
articles.excerpt: Wells Fargo's IBIT shares doubled to 49.6 million. A 13F can't say whose money it is, and bitcoin has fallen about 22% since Sept. 30.
articles.body_md:
Seven of the biggest banks that file with the SEC reported a combined $5.49 billion of BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) on Sept. 30, their quarterly 13F filings show. Wells Fargo alone listed $2.35 billion in a [filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000342/13F_9_2026.xml) made Monday, the last day for third-quarter reports.

Those numbers are seven weeks old. Bitcoin traded at $65,034 at 8:12 a.m. ET Tuesday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), about 22% below its Sept. 30 level near $83,600. A [Coindaro review](https://www.coindaro.com/banks-13f-bitcoin-etf-wells-fargo-goldman-xrp/) of the filings puts the drop at 22% too.

**The bank-by-bank count**

IBIT shares reported on Sept. 30, against June 30, from each bank's 13F and Coindaro's tally of the same filings:

- [Wells Fargo](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000342/13F_9_2026.xml): 49.58 million shares worth $2.35 billion, up from 24.40 million
- [Morgan Stanley](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/895421/000089542126000309/US_13F-408-20260930.xml): 19.52 million, $923.9 million, up from 16.48 million
- [Goldman Sachs](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886982/000088698226000647/Submit_this.xml): 16.44 million, $778.3 million, down from 17.23 million
- [Bank of America](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/70858/000007085826000589/Q3202613FHR.xml): 14.48 million, $685.4 million, up from 1.72 million
- [JPMorgan](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/19617/000001961726000404/Information_Table_09.30.2026.xml): 11.41 million, $540.0 million, up from 10.41 million
- [Barclays](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/312069/000031206926000241/13fInfoTable_09302026.xml): 3.94 million, $186.7 million, up from 2.66 million
- [Citigroup](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000083100126000052/CITIGROUP_13F_HR_INFOTABLE.xml): 521,144 shares, $24.7 million, up from 347,114

Bitcoin rose about 42% over the quarter, so dollar values grew faster than share counts. Share counts are the cleaner gauge of buying. Goldman's count fell 4.6% while the value of its line rose 36%. JPMorgan's 9.6% rise and its $540 million figure match [The Block's report](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-13-jpmorgan-reports-36-rise-in-strategy-share-holdings-and-540-million-in-blackrocks-bitcoin-etf-439671).

**IBIT isn't the only fund**

Goldman also listed 5.48 million shares of Fidelity's Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund, worth $397.9 million, up from 105,840 in June. Its spot bitcoin funds came to about $1.28 billion in all, Coindaro and [CoinNess](https://coinness.com/en/news/1175857) reported.

Morgan Stanley reported 6.72 million shares of its own Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust (MSBT), worth $160.9 million. Its asset management arm [launched that fund](https://www.morganstanley.com/press-releases/msim-enters-with-launch-of-morgan-stanley-bitcoin-trust) in April with a 0.14% fee, the lowest among bitcoin funds at the time, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/04/08/morgan-stanley-s-bitcoin-etf-opens-today-giving-blackrock-s-usd55-billion-ibit-fund-its-toughest-rival-yet) reported. The filing doesn't say whether those shares are seed money.

Bank of America's eightfold jump came after a policy change. Since Jan. 5, its Merrill, Private Bank and Merrill Edge advisers can recommend four spot bitcoin funds, IBIT among them, at 1% to 4% of a portfolio, [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bank-america-expands-crypto-access-wealth-management-clients-2025-12-04/) and [WealthManagement.com](https://www.wealthmanagement.com/crypto/bank-of-america-broadens-access-to-crypto-funds) reported. The filing itself doesn't give a reason for the change.

**How it works: four ways a bank touches bitcoin**

A spot bitcoin ETF holds real bitcoin and trades on a stock exchange, so a buyer gets the price moves without handling coins or private keys. A bank can sit next to that exposure in four different ways:

- For clients: advisers or a trust arm buy the fund in customer accounts. The customer keeps the gains and losses.
- For itself: the bank's own capital is at risk.
- Market making: a trading desk buys and sells to fill client orders and can hedge with options, so it may hold shares with little net bet.
- Custody: the bank guards coins or keys for someone else for a fee, as BNY does for MSBT. It doesn't own the bitcoin.

**What a 13F shows, and what it hides**

A manager with discretion over at least $100 million of listed U.S. securities must report its long positions on the last day of each quarter within 45 days, the [SEC's guidance](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/division-investment-management-frequently-asked-questions/frequently-asked-questions-about-form-13f) says. Short sales, futures and swaps aren't on it. Options appear only as share counts marked "put" or "call," with no strike or expiry date. So a 13F can't show whose money it is or whether a position is hedged. Wells Fargo "isn't necessarily making a multibillion-dollar bitcoin bet," [CoinDesk wrote](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/17/wells-fargo-s-reported-blackrock-bitcoin-etf-holdings-double-to-usd2-35-billion).

The options lines point to trading desks. Barclays listed 3.94 million IBIT shares beside calls on 8.48 million and puts on 8.17 million, its filing and [AiTraderView](https://aitraderview.com/2026/11/10/barclays-lifts-ibit-position-48-to-3-94-million-shares-in-latest-13f-filing/) show. Goldman reported puts on 7.51 million shares, and JPMorgan calls on 3.70 million and puts on 2.92 million.

**Why banks hold the fund, not the coin**

Owning bitcoin outright is expensive for a bank. The Basel Committee's [crypto standard](https://www.bis.org/bcbs/publ/d545.htm) gives unbacked tokens such as bitcoin a 1,250% risk weight. At the 8% minimum, that means a dollar of capital for every dollar of bitcoin, according to [CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/outdated-bank-rules-may-keep-crypto-outside-the-banks-now-allowed-to-hold-it/). The committee agreed in November 2025 to speed up a review of that standard and [said Oct. 1](https://www.bis.org/media-releases/20261001-basel-committee-meets-advance-supervisory-and-regulatory-initiatives-and-discuss-risks-and) it expects to give an update by year-end.

**What changed in the U.S. rules**

- Jan. 23, 2025: the SEC's [SAB 122](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/staff-accounting-bulletins/staff-accounting-bulletin-122) rescinded SAB 121, which had made firms holding crypto for customers book it as a liability on their own balance sheets, [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/wall-street-regulator-revokes-accounting-guidance-crypto-assets-2025-01-24/) reported. That had made custody costly for banks.
- March 7, 2025: the OCC's [Interpretive Letter 1183](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-16.html) dropped the need for a supervisory non-objection before national banks offer crypto custody.
- March 28, 2025: the [FDIC said](https://www.fdic.gov/news/press-releases/2025/fdic-clarifies-process-banks-engage-crypto-related-activities) its banks no longer need prior approval for permissible crypto activities.
- April 24, 2025: the [Fed withdrew](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/bcreg20250424a.htm) its advance-notice letter and, with the FDIC, two 2023 warnings on crypto risk, [Sullivan & Cromwell](https://www.sullcrom.com/SullivanCromwell/_Assets/PDFs/Memos/Federal-Reserve-Board-FDIC-Withdraw-Crypto-Asset-Activities-Guidance.pdf) wrote, putting all three regulators on the same footing.
- Dec. 9, 2025: [Interpretive Letter 1188](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-121.html) let national banks act as "riskless principal," buying bitcoin from one customer only against an offsetting sale to another, [Jones Day](https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2025/12/occ-confirms-riskless-principal-transactions-in-crypto-assets-by-banks-are-permissible) said.

**From funds to the coin itself**

Some banks now handle bitcoin directly. PNC began spot bitcoin trading for Private Bank clients on Dec. 9, 2025, through Coinbase, its [release](https://pnc.mediaroom.com/2025-12-09-PNC-First-Major-Bank-to-Launch-Direct-Bitcoin-Access-for-Clients,-Powered-by-Coinbases-Crypto-as-a-Service-Infrastructure) and [American Banker](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/pnc-launches-direct-crypto-trading-through-coinbase) show. E*Trade finished rolling out bitcoin, ether and solana trading through Zerohash on July 16, [Morgan Stanley](https://www.morganstanley.com/press-releases/etrade-completes-crypto-spot-trading-rollout) and [Ledger Insights](https://www.ledgerinsights.com/morgan-stanleys-etrade-goes-live-with-crypto-trading/) reported.

The OCC gave preliminary conditional approval on June 18 to Morgan Stanley Digital Trust, a national trust bank for crypto custody and staking, its [decision letter](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/interpretations-and-decisions/2026/cd1378.pdf) and [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/morgan-stanley-occ-conditional-approval-trust-bank-charter-digital-assets-zerohash-gould/823961/) show. It can't open until it gets final approval. Citi said in August it will add bitcoin custody to its [Custody+](https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2026/citi-custody-plus-suite-near-real-time-custody-solutions) platform this year, without a date, [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/08/18/citi-plans-to-launch-bitcoin-custody-for-institutional-clients-later-this-year).

Abroad, Deutsche Bank opened bitcoin and ether custody to institutional and corporate clients in Europe after approval from Germany's BaFin, [the bank](https://corporates.db.com/more/latest-news/deutsche-bank-launches-digital-asset-custody-solution-for-institutional-and-corporate-clients) and [Bitcoin Magazine](https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/deutsche-bank-bitcoin-custody-live) said Nov. 11. Standard Chartered began spot bitcoin and ether trading for institutions in July 2025, [its release](https://www.sc.com/en/press-release/standard-chartered-launches-digital-assets-trading-for-institutional-clients/) and [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/stanchart-launches-bitcoin-ether-spot-trading-institutional-clients-2025-07-15/) show.

**What to watch**

The next 13Fs, covering Dec. 31, are due Feb. 16, 2027, once the 45-day deadline rolls past a weekend and Presidents Day. They will be the first to show what bank accounts did during bitcoin's slide. The Basel update is due by year-end, and Citi still owes a custody start date.

*In our opinion: Bank of America's share count, up from 1.72 million to 14.48 million, tells more than Wells Fargo's bigger dollar figure, because it shows what happens when advisers get permission to recommend the funds. The ETF wrapper exists in part because Basel's 1,250% weight makes owning the coin so costly for banks. If the year-end review eases that charge, more bitcoin could move from client accounts onto bank balance sheets. The Feb. 16 filings will show whether those accounts held on through a quarter in which bitcoin has lost more than a fifth.*

articles.title: Optimizely Breach Put Wallet-Swapping Code on 178 Sites, Including Ledger
articles.excerpt: The injected script swapped crypto addresses on pages from HSBC, Ledger, Zoom and others on Nov. 16. Wallets tied to it took in about $7,040, Report URI said.
articles.body_md:
An attacker slipped crypto-stealing code into websites run by 178 organizations on Monday, Nov. 16, through a flaw in Optimizely's web-testing service. The affected sites included hardware wallet maker Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN, according to security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI, as summarized by [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) and [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hijacked-optimizely-scripts-served-card.html).

Optimizely said an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation product and added malicious JavaScript to some customer projects, [StepSecurity](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/optimjack-optimizely-hosted-scripts-crypto-clipper-card-skimmer) reported, citing the company's status page. Optimizely said it fixed the flaw, removed the code and secured affected accounts.

### How the script stole crypto

Many sites load small scripts from outside vendors to run tests and track visitors. Here, the attacker wrote code into a custom field in each Optimizely project, so it rode along on every page of every affected site without touching the sites' own servers.

The script looked for crypto addresses on eight networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron. When it found one near a word like "wallet," "deposit" or "send," it swapped in the attacker's address, including in text a visitor copied to the clipboard. Because the replacement passed the chain's checksum, a wallet app would accept it. It also tried to skim card numbers typed into checkout forms and loaded exploit kits aimed at iPhones, [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/optimizely-supply-chain-attack-infects-major-brands-sites-with-malware/) and StepSecurity said.

Helme found the code in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely snippets he checked, and said the real count is likely higher. Six of the organizations are crypto or trading firms and 32 are banks or financial companies.

Wallets hard-coded in the script had received about $7,040 within roughly nine hours, Report URI estimated, per [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hijacked-optimizely-scripts-served-card.html). StepSecurity put the total near $6,600 and noted that two addresses were in use before the attack, so not every transfer can be tied to a victim. It said the attacker emptied the bitcoin, ether and litecoin wallets early Tuesday, UTC.

Ledger and HSBC had not commented in the reports reviewed by Black Mint as of 5:50 a.m. ET.

*In our opinion: The dollar figure is small. The reach is not, because one vendor account pushed code to 178 brands at once. Anyone who copied a deposit address from an affected site on Nov. 16 should compare it character by character with the address shown in their own wallet or exchange account before sending again.*

articles.title: Wells Fargo Reports $2.35 Billion in BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF, Up From $812 Million
articles.excerpt: Wells Fargo's 13F shows 49.58 million IBIT shares on Sept. 30, about double June's count. The filing includes client accounts, not just the bank's own money.
articles.body_md:
Wells Fargo reported 49.58 million shares of BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $2.35 billion at the end of September, up from 24.40 million shares worth $812 million three months earlier, according to its [quarterly 13F filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000342/13F_9_2026.xml) made Monday, Nov. 16. The share count roughly doubled. The dollar value nearly tripled.

The gap between those two numbers is mostly price. Bitcoin rose about 42% from June 30 to Sept. 30, based on BlackRock's figures, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/17/wells-fargo-s-reported-blackrock-bitcoin-etf-holdings-double-to-usd2-35-billion) reported. The same filing also lists options on IBIT: calls covering 717,200 shares and puts covering 540,000 shares.

### What a 13F does and doesn't show

A 13F is a snapshot that large investment managers file with the SEC 45 days after each quarter ends, listing the U.S.-traded stocks and funds they oversee. Wells Fargo's filing covers the bank and several of its investment managers, and many of the positions sit in accounts run for clients. So it tells readers how much IBIT runs through the Wells Fargo system, not how much bitcoin exposure the bank carries on its own balance sheet. The [June-quarter filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000304/13F_6_2026.xml) gives the earlier figures.

CoinDesk estimated the position equals about 28,070 bitcoin, based on IBIT holding 801,033 BTC against 1.415 billion shares on Sept. 30.

The numbers are seven weeks old. Bitcoin traded at $64,212 at 5:52 a.m. ET Tuesday, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), down 0.4% in 24 hours. The filing says nothing about whether those accounts bought or sold since.

*In our opinion: The more telling detail is the 103% jump in share count. Price alone can't explain that, so the bank's advisers and clients were adding IBIT through the summer. The next real check is the December-quarter 13F, due in mid-February, which will show what they did during the slide.*

articles.title: CFTC Approves Backpack's U.S. Exchange and Clearinghouse for Crypto Perps
articles.excerpt: The CFTC designated Backpack's exchange on Nov. 16, three days after registering its clearinghouse. No U.S. launch date has been set.
articles.body_md:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved Backpack's U.S. derivatives exchange on Monday, Nov. 16, three days after it registered the firm's clearinghouse. That gives the crypto company both federal licenses it needs to offer leveraged perpetual futures to American traders. It has not said when trading starts.

The agency designated TLD Markets, Inc., which does business as Backpack Exchange, as a contract market in an [order of designation](https://www.cftc.gov/filings/documents/2026/orgdcmtldbackpackord261116.pdf) dated Nov. 16. Its affiliate, TLD Clearing, Inc., or Backpack Clearing, was registered on Nov. 13 to clear margined futures and fully collateralized futures, options on futures and swaps, the [CFTC's clearinghouse registry](https://www.cftc.gov/IndustryOversight/IndustryFilings/ClearingOrganizations) shows.

### Two licenses, two jobs

A designated contract market is a federally supervised exchange that can list futures and options. A derivatives clearing organization is the clearinghouse behind it: it stands between buyer and seller on each trade, collects margin and guarantees settlement if one side can't pay. Perpetual futures, the product Backpack plans to list, are futures with no expiry date, so a trader can hold a leveraged position open as long as margin holds up.

Backpack said in a [press release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/16/3404185/0/en/backpack-receives-landmark-cftc-approval-to-establish-first-ever-blockchain-based-derivatives-exchange-in-the-united-states-with-global-unified-liquidity.html) that U.S. users will be able to trade those contracts 24/7, post cash or crypto as collateral, cross-margin positions and trade in the same global order book as its overseas customers. The company called it the first blockchain-based derivatives exchange in the U.S. and said it serves users in more than 150 countries and regions, with more than $450 billion in trading volume. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/cftc-approves-backpack-s-blockchain-derivatives-venue) reported the U.S. service is still taking waitlist sign-ups.

"From a policy perspective this is a really big deal," said Mark Wetjen, president of Backpack US, adding that it moves "price discovery from offshore unregulated venues to the United States."

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a [statement](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/SpeechesTestimony/seligstatement111626) that the law sets core principles "without prescribing a particular technological architecture." He added that firms built on blockchains must meet the same standards as everyone else, including anti-money laundering programs, segregation of customer funds, market surveillance and system safeguards.

*In our opinion: Backpack's pitch is that leveraged crypto trading belongs onshore, under a U.S. regulator's rules on margin and customer money. It now holds both licenses to test that idea. The paperwork is done, but the order book is still a waitlist, so the launch date and how much volume shows up are the numbers to watch.*

articles.title: New Zealand Forecasters Lift One-Year Inflation Outlook to 2.92%
articles.excerpt: One-year expectations jumped 32 basis points in the RBNZ survey, while five- and 10-year views eased. Forecasters see the cash rate at 3.40% in a year.
articles.body_md:
New Zealand's business leaders and professional forecasters now expect inflation of 2.92% a year from now, up from 2.60% three months ago, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's [Survey of Expectations](https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/-/media/project/sites/rbnz/files/statistics/series/m/m14/insights/2026/survey-of-expectations-november-2026.pdf) showed on Tuesday, Nov. 17, local time. That is a 32-basis-point jump in one quarter.

The longer view moved the other way. Two-year expectations edged up to 2.36% from 2.34%, five-year expectations fell to 2.17% from 2.31%, and 10-year expectations slipped to 2.13% from 2.20%, according to the survey and [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/new-zealand/inflation-expectations/news/601736).

### What the survey measures

Every quarter the central bank asks a panel of executives and economists where they think prices, wages and interest rates are heading. This round drew 44 responses, collected from Oct. 23 to 30. The two-year figure gets the most attention because that is roughly when a rate change made today works its way into prices, [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/rbnz-survey-nz-two-year-inflation-expectations-rise-to-236-qoq-in-q4-2026-202611170203) noted. Expectations matter on their own, too: a firm that expects higher costs tends to raise prices and wages in advance.

Respondents also lifted their rate forecast. They see the Official Cash Rate at 3.40% a year from now, up from 3.21% in the last survey, and at 3.05% by the end of December. Actual inflation was 3.7% in the September quarter, down from 4.1% in June, and unemployment rose to 5.7%, the RBNZ said.

For markets, the survey adds New Zealand to a list of places where rate expectations are climbing. Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said on Sunday the Fed "has some work to do on inflation," [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/fed-has-some-work-to-do-on-inflation-kansas-city-fed-chief-says.html) reported. Higher expected rates raise the return on cash and bonds, which compete for the same money as assets with no yield, such as bitcoin.

*In our opinion: The split is the real story. Forecasters see a bumpier year ahead but still trust the long run, with 10-year expectations at 2.13%, close to the RBNZ's 2% target midpoint. Borrowers carry the stake, since the one-year cash-rate forecast rose 19 basis points in a single survey. The next check is the central bank's own rate decision and whether it sounds as worried as its panel.*

articles.title: Strategy's Debt and Preferred Stock Cost $1.43 Billion a Year
articles.excerpt: Its 850,849 bitcoin cost $75,452 each, above Monday's price. A $4.75 billion cash reserve covers about 40 months of interest and dividends.
articles.body_md:
Strategy needs about $1.43 billion a year to cover interest on its convertible notes and dividends on five preferred stocks, its [Nov. 15 investor briefing](https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltf8d808d9b8cebd37/blt36fbde4f9ee6bd70/6afa7fcf5a0d255dea73ad18/MSTR_Investor_Briefing_As_of_2026-11-15.pdf) shows. Its 850,849 bitcoin sat below cost Monday.

**How the borrowing works**

A convertible note is a loan the lender can swap for stock at a set price, so it carries a low coupon. Perpetual preferred stock never matures. It pays a fixed dividend ahead of common shareholders, and if it's "cumulative," a skipped payment piles up and must be paid before common holders get anything.

**850,849 coins bought over six years**

The company paid $64.20 billion for its coins, or $75,452 each including fees, its [Nov. 16 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/0001193125-26-462151.txt) shows. It held 70,469 at the end of 2020 and 447,470 at the end of 2024, earlier filings show. With bitcoin at $64,922 at 3:42 p.m. ET Monday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), the stack was worth about $55.2 billion, roughly $9 billion under cost. That loss stays on paper unless coins are sold.

**$6.71 billion of notes, mostly at 0%**

Six series were outstanding on Sept. 30, the [quarterly filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000060/mstr-20260930.htm) shows. Each lets holders demand cash on a put date:

- $1.01 billion at 0.625%, due 2028, put Sept. 15, 2027, converts at $183.19
- $1.5 billion at 0%, due 2029, put June 1, 2028, converts at $672.40
- $2 billion at 0%, due 2030, put March 1, 2028, converts at $433.43
- $800 million at 0.625%, due 2030, put Sept. 15, 2028, converts at $149.77
- $603.7 million at 0.875%, due 2031, put Sept. 15, 2028, converts at $232.72
- $800 million at 2.25%, due 2032, put June 15, 2029, converts at $204.33

Coupons cost about $34.6 million a year. MSTR traded near $103.32 at 3:43 p.m. ET, per Yahoo Finance, below every conversion price.

**The preferred bill is the big one**

Rates are from the 10-Q; the STRC count subtracts weekly buybacks since Oct. 25:

- STRC: 12%, cumulative, paid daily; about 77.6 million shares, roughly $932 million a year
- STRD: 10%, not cumulative; $140.2 million
- STRF: 10%, cumulative; $128.4 million
- STRK: 8%, cumulative, payable in cash or stock; $112.2 million
- STRE: 10% in euros, cumulative; €77.5 million, about $85 million

With coupons, that's about $1.43 billion, matching Strategy's figure.

**Where the money comes from**

Software won't cover it. Third-quarter revenue was $125.4 million, and the 10-Q says software cash isn't expected to meet the company's needs.

The USD Reserve held $4.75 billion on Nov. 15, plus $151.2 million of USD Cash, the 8-K says. Board policy keeps at least 12 months of payments in it. At $1.43 billion a year, the reserve alone covers about 40 months. Strategy puts both pools at 3.42 years.

New stock fills the rest. Strategy sold $244.7 million of MSTR shares last week and has $18.09 billion of sales capacity left.

It has also sold bitcoin: about 6,947 coins this year for $431.8 million, to fund dividends and STRC buybacks, the 10-Q and its [Oct. 29 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000105044626000047/mstr-20261029x8kxex9912.htm) show.

**mNAV and a falling bitcoin**

mNAV is Strategy's share price divided by its bitcoin per share after debt and preferred claims, net of cash. It was 1.09x at Nov. 13 prices, the briefing and [strategy.com](https://www.strategy.com/) show. Our recalculation at Monday afternoon prices gives about 1.1x.

Near or below 1x, new MSTR sales add less per share. The briefing warns that issuance "below appropriate value can reduce Net BPS." A deeper bitcoin slide thins the cushion behind the preferred. STRC traded as low as about $71 in June, the 10-Q says.

**Rates set the price of money**

The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, [its statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm) shows, and meets again Dec. 8-9. STRC pays about eight points over that. Interest on Strategy's cash paid for $21.8 million of last week's STRC buybacks. Rate cuts would shrink that income.

*In our opinion: the yearly bill looks covered for now, with about 40 months of reserve and no new stock sold. The harder stretch starts in September 2027, when holders can demand cash for $1.01 billion of notes, then $4.9 billion more in 2028. Every series converts above Monday's share price. The number to check each Monday is mNAV in the 8-K and on strategy.com, since it decides whether new stock or bitcoin sales pay the bill.*

articles.title: Judge Acquits Peraire-Bueno Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum MEV Case
articles.excerpt: A year after a jury deadlocked, Judge Jessica Clarke ruled prosecutors showed no material misrepresentation, so wire fraud convictions couldn't stand.
articles.body_md:
A federal judge in Manhattan on Monday acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno, the MIT-educated brothers charged over $25 million in crypto taken from Ethereum trading bots in about 12 seconds in April 2023.

U.S. District Judge Jessica Clarke granted the brothers' motion for acquittal. She found prosecutors had not shown at trial that the pair made any material misrepresentation, which wire fraud requires, [Reuters reported](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-915104). [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/business-and-practice/mit-brothers-acquitted-in-25-million-crypto-case-avoid-retrial) reported the ruling means the brothers avoid a retrial. A jury deadlocked on every count in November 2025, and Clarke declared a mistrial then.

"The question before the court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes," Clarke wrote, according to Reuters. She added that the transactions "were not placed on a regulated market with rules prohibiting this conduct."

**How the trade worked**

MEV, or maximal extractable value, is the extra profit available from choosing which transactions go into a block and in what order, per [ethereum.org](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/mev/). Automated "sandwich" bots chase it by trading just before and just after another user's trade.

Prosecutors said the brothers used bait transactions to lure those bots, then exploited a flaw in MEV-Boost, software most Ethereum validators run to receive blocks from outside builders, to swap in their own transactions and drain the bots. The defense argued it was a legitimate trading strategy. The brothers were indicted in May 2024, and Reuters said no scheme of this type had been federally prosecuted before.

A spokesperson for U.S. Attorney James McDonald's office declined to comment, and the brothers' lawyers had no immediate comment, Reuters said.

*In our opinion: the ruling is narrow. Clarke tested the case against wire fraud only, and her own words leave room for "uncharged crimes." For MEV searchers and the validators they pay, the open question is where code-exploiting trades sit in U.S. law. On this record, wire fraud wasn't the answer.*

articles.title: Nasdaq Drops 2.5% as Nvidia Slide Drags Tech, Bitcoin Holds Near $65,400
articles.excerpt: Nvidia fell 4.1% to $156.14 ahead of Tuesday's earnings, and the S&P 500 lost 1.9% for a third straight drop. Bitcoin was up 0.4% over 24 hours.
articles.body_md:
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49% on Monday to 24,509.76, its third straight loss, as Nvidia led another sell-off in chip and AI stocks.

The S&P 500 lost 1.92% to 7,416.59 and the Dow fell 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/15/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-ai-nvidia-oil-us-35786b8f539ec95f16ae0500f71cfcc7). Bitcoin went the other way, barely. It sat at $65,429 at 5:47 p.m. ET, up 0.4% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko. Ether was at $1,832, up 0.3%.

**Nvidia's slide since October**

Nvidia closed at $156.14, down 4.12%, [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stocks-lower-at-close-of-trade-dow-jones-industrial-average-down-141-5030993) data show. That is about 35% below its record close of $239.24 on Oct. 6, [The Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/11/16/stock-market-drops-amid-continued-nvidia-fallout/) reported. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week. The company reports third-quarter results after Tuesday's close.

The selling spread. Micron fell 7.62% and Intel 7.07%, and Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan each lost more than 2%, per CNBC. Falling stocks beat rising ones on the NYSE by 2,197 to 655.

**Why chip stocks matter to crypto**

Nvidia sits at the center of what traders call the AI trade, and CNBC said Tuesday's results will be judged as much on how the company moves forward after Huang's exit as on the numbers. Crypto feels it through the same pool of investors: a sell-off that cuts tech portfolios can leave less appetite for other volatile assets. On Monday, that spillover didn't show up in bitcoin's price.

Bitcoin had already taken its hit. It fell to about $62,000 late Saturday, its lowest since August, after forced selling of leveraged bets, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/bitcoin-slides-to-62000-following-liquidation-cascade-then-rebounds-slightly.html). The Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 10, or "Extreme Fear," on Monday.

*In our opinion: on a 2.5% down day for the Nasdaq, bitcoin was the calm one in the room while chip stocks took the losses. That split lasted one session, with a Fear & Greed reading of 10 behind it. The bigger test is Tuesday night, when Nvidia's numbers land with a new leadership story attached. The number to watch is bitcoin's Saturday low near $62,000, and whether Monday's split survives Wednesday's open.*

articles.title: Four Democratic Senators Press SEC on Tokenized Stock Exemption's AML Gaps
articles.excerpt: The senators asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins how know-your-customer rules apply when tokenized shares move to unverified wallets. The SEC declined to comment.
articles.body_md:
Four Democratic senators asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins on Monday to explain how anti-money-laundering rules apply under the agency's five-year exemption for tokenized stock trading, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-16-democratic-senators-warn-secs-tokenized-stock-exemption-illicit-finance-gaps-441432) and [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/regulation/58817) reported.

Sens. Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto signed the letter.

**What the exemption allows**

A tokenized stock is a blockchain token that represents a share of a company. It can move between wallets. The SEC's innovation exemption, launched in September, lets qualifying "tokenized securities venues" trade these tokens for up to five years without registering as a national securities exchange, both outlets reported.

Know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering (AML) rules require platforms to verify who their customers are and watch for suspicious money. The senators said the exemption doesn't spell out how those checks apply to trades, or whether a venue must limit who can receive a token. Their concern: a buyer who passed identity checks could send the token to an unverified wallet, including one held by a foreign person or someone engaged in illegal activity, outside U.S. oversight.

**Pricing, opt-outs and rulemaking**

The letter also raised retail pricing protections and said companies should be able to opt out of having their stock tokenized. The senators asked how the SEC will enforce AML standards and check platforms' disclosures and self-verification, and they asked that any further changes come through a formal, public rulemaking.

Formal rulemaking means the SEC would publish a proposal and take public comment before a rule is final, unlike an exemption the agency can grant on its own.

The SEC declined to comment on the letter, The Block said.

Strategy bought 485 bitcoin for $33.4 million last week, its 8-K filing shows, while its full 850,849-coin holding sat about $9.3 billion below what the company paid for it.

The company's average cost is $75,452 per coin, or $64.20 billion in total, as of Nov. 15. With bitcoin near $64,550 at 11:45 a.m. ET Monday, per CoinGecko, the stack was worth about $54.9 billion. That gap is on paper. It becomes a realized loss only if Strategy sells.

**Most of the new cash went to preferred stock**

Strategy sold 2,087,040 shares of its MSTR common stock between Nov. 9 and Nov. 15 through an at-the-market program, raising $244.7 million after commissions. Only $33.4 million of it bought bitcoin, at an average of $68,887 each. Another $206.3 million went to repurchasing its STRC preferred stock, and $5 million went to cash, the filing says.

An at-the-market program lets a company sell new shares into the market a little at a time, at current prices, instead of in one large offering. STRC is Strategy's variable-rate perpetual preferred stock: it pays holders a dividend and has no maturity date. Buying it back cuts the number of those shares outstanding.

**Bitcoin's slide sets the backdrop**

Bitcoin fell as low as about $62,000 late Saturday, its lowest since August, per Coin Metrics data cited by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/bitcoin-slides-to-62000-following-liquidation-cascade-then-rebounds-slightly.html). Strategy wasn't the only treasury company buying. Bitmine Immersion said Monday it added 7,653 ether last week and now holds 6,077,745 ETH.
